newsitem.title: USA: Brent up in late US trading, foreign crudes abound.
newsitem.headline: Brent up in late US trading, foreign crudes abound.

text.p: North Sea Brent was up in late U.S. trading Tuesday featuring a variety of U.S. and European dealers, traders said.

A full boat of March Brent changed hands at $22.33 a barrel, up from $22.24 a barrel at the IPE settlement in London. Five partials totalling 500 lots traded at $22.25/22.29/22.30/22.32 a barrel, traders said.
A second full boat of April Brent traded at $21.90 a barrel, up 16 cents from the London close, traders said.
March/April Brent moved at 42 cents a barrel, down eight cents from the IPE close.
Meanwhile, the U.S. Gulf Coast continues to attract Brent cargoes, thanks to the wide open transatlantic arbitrage.
The spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and Brent for March stood around $1.70-80 a barrel, giving sellers ample economic incentive to move cargoes eastward, traders said.
A U.S. broker was heard to have sold one million barrels of Brent to a U.S. Gulf Coast refiner around March WTI minus 40 cents a barrel. Delivery is slated for March 10-15, traders said.
At least three other companies are offering Brents in the same first-half March window, although traders said only two refiners were still looking in that period.
"A lot of this is just busy talk to see where the market is," said one trader, expressing skepticism about whether the offers would actually get done.
From West Africa, two companies are showing Nigerian Qua Iboe cargoes for delivery into the Gulf Coast for late February and mid-March, with the latter on offer at WTI plus 35 cents.
One dealer doubted that refiners would pick up the Qua Iboe cargoes at that price, which is 75 cents over the going Brent rate. "The spread outweighs the quality difference," he said.
